items.title: Hippocampal reactivation of aversive experience promotes a slow-breathing recovery state
items.author: Karim Benchenane
items.content: Mahéo, Bagur et al. show that after escaping danger, mice enter a distinct slow-breathing state that promotes recovery from stress, revealing that recovery is an active physiological process rather than a passive return to baseline.

items.title: The identity gene Fezf2 is repurposed postnatally to specify inhibitory input in an activity-dependent manner
items.author: Beatriz Rico
items.content: Kroon et al. show that Fezf2, the gene that gives a cortical neuron its identity before birth, is reused postnatally under the control of neuronal activity to set how much inhibition that neuron receives.

items.title: Highly selective visual circuits in mouse frontal cortex
items.author: Bilal Haider
items.content: The authors identify neurons in the frontal cortex of awake mice with highly selective visual receptive fields. These neurons prioritize encoding of binocular visual space, require V1 input and provide functional feedback throughout the visual cortex.

items.title: Presynaptic functional organization by phase separation
items.author: Shigeki Watanabe
items.content: This Review by Ogunmowo and Watanabe summarizes recent findings in the field showing how presynaptic functions are enabled, organized and coordinated by phase separation and discusses future directions in this branch of neuroscience.

items.title: A shared meaning component across languages in the human brain
items.author: Evelina Fedorenko
items.content: Using fMRI data from speakers of 21 languages and multilingual language models, de Varda et al. show that brain encoding models trained on some languages predict responses to unseen languages, pointing to a shared meaning component across languages.

items.title: Neotenic expansion of adult-born dentate granule cells reconfigures GABAergic inhibition to enhance social memory consolidation
items.author: Amar Sahay
items.content: This study describes a circuit mechanism by which immature adult-born dentate granule cells promote network oscillations to support memory consolidation.
